title: Gemstone Lights vs a DIY Track Lighting Kit
metaTitle: Gemstone Lights vs a DIY Track Lighting Kit in Canada
metaDescription: Gemstone Lights is dealer-installed with a lifetime warranty on its lights. A DIY track kit is posted-price hardware you mount yourself. A fair comparison.
excerpt: Gemstone Lights and a DIY track kit are the same kind of hardware bought two different ways. Here is what Gemstone publishes, what it does not, and how a boxed kit compares on warranty, cold rating and price.
heroAlt: Large two-storey home lit in warm white permanent track lighting at night
keyTakeaways: Gemstone Lights is sold and installed only through authorized dealers. Its FAQ says it does not offer a DIY version of its track system.
Gemstone publishes 12V, RGBWW, 9 inch spacing, IP67 and 46 lumens per light, but no price and no cold rating in degrees.
Gemstone's warranty is longer than ours: lifetime on track lights and 10 years on system parts, against our 5 years on parts.
A DIY track kit is a posted-price box you mount yourself with a drill and a ladder. See current kit prices at /diy-kits
We found no Gemstone price per foot published in CA$. Dealers quote each house.

body.text: Short answer: Gemstone Lights and our kits are the same kind of hardware, 12V lights sitting in an aluminum track under the eaves. The difference is how you buy it. Gemstone sells only through authorized dealers who install it for you, with a lifetime warranty on the lights and no published price. Our kits are sold by the box at a posted price, you mount them yourself with a drill and a ladder, and the warranty is 5 years on parts. If you want someone else on the ladder and the longer warranty, Gemstone is a fair choice. If you want to see the price before anyone visits and you are happy to do the work, a kit is.

Gemstone was founded in Calgary and describes itself as Canadian owned. It sells through authorized dealers across North America, and its FAQ is direct about DIY: "We do not offer a DIY solution for the Gemstone Lights Track Lighting System." The numbers below come from that FAQ and from Gemstone's Track and Light Guide dated June 2023, which one of its Ontario dealers hosts as a PDF.

items: Light type: RGBWW, which Gemstone defines as red, green, blue and a dedicated warm white. White is adjustable from 2800K to 7000K.
Brightness: 46 lumens per light at maximum, or 60 to 100 lumens per foot.
Power: 0.96 W per light at most.
Track: aluminum, colour-matched to over 150 soffit and fascia colours.
Certification: ETL or UL, approved for sale in the United States and Canada.
Rated life: 50,000 hours, which Gemstone works out to about 20 years at 7 hours a day.

body.text: Control is through the Gemstone Lights app and a hub. The FAQ lists support for 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz WiFi, a local Bluetooth connection when WiFi is down, and on and off control through Google Home or Amazon Alexa. It also says: "There are no monthly fees for using the Gemstone Lights app."

items: A price. The FAQ says cost depends on linear footage and local installation rates, and that exact pricing comes from a dealer quote. We found no price per foot published in CA$.
A cold rating in degrees. The guide lists operating temperature as "All North American Climates" and the FAQ says the system was designed to withstand Calgary's winters. No figure is given.
A labour warranty. The manufacturer's warranty does not cover labour. Each dealer sets its own.

body.text: The one dealer figure we found: Blingle Premier Lighting of Northern Colorado, a Gemstone dealer, posted "$28 per linear foot" as its fall 2026 price, rising to $29 on 1 December 2026 (currency not stated, a US dealer; as listed on 27 November 2026). That is one dealer in one US market. It is not a Canadian quote.
Warranty: Gemstone's is longer than ours

We will say this plainly. Gemstone's FAQ lists a lifetime warranty on its track lights and 10 years on system parts. Systems installed before 1 October 2024 keep the original 5-year warranty. Our warranty is 5 years on parts. We are not a dealer network and we do not offer a lifetime warranty. With a DIY kit you are also the installer, so there is no labour warranty to ask about. With Gemstone, ask the dealer what labour cover they add and for how long, because that part is theirs, not Gemstone's.

body.text: What you get in a DIY track kit

Our lights are 12V RGBW and press into aluminum track. Each track piece is 42 inches long and holds five lights, about 8 inches apart. Track comes in black, white, wicker or brown. That is four colours against Gemstone's 150 plus, so if an exact match to an unusual soffit matters, Gemstone has more to choose from.

Kits are sized at 50, 75, 100, 150, 200 and 250 ft, and power injection parts are included in kits of 100 ft and up. The power supply is a 12V Class 2 unit that plugs into an outdoor GFCI outlet. The controller joins your WiFi, runs WLED, and works with a free app on Android and iPhone. Scenes keep running if the internet drops. You can see how the parts go together at /how-it-works before you buy anything.

Gemstone's guide says each lamp has a threaded waterproof connector and can be removed and replaced on its own, and it tells owners to contact their authorized dealer for that work. With our kits every part is also sold separately at /shop so you can swap one light, one track piece or one connector yourself. Neither approach is wrong. One sends a dealer back up the ladder, the other sends you.

items: Gemstone Lights is a good fit if you want a dealer to measure, colour-match and install the system, you value a lifetime warranty on the lights, and you are comfortable getting a quote and not reading a price list.
A DIY track kit is a good fit if you are comfortable with a drill and a ladder, you want the price in front of you before you commit, and a 5-year parts warranty is enough for you.
Our installed service is a good fit if you live in Southwestern Ontario and want this hardware put up by our own crew.

faq.q: Can I buy Gemstone Lights and install them myself?
faq.a: No. Gemstone's FAQ says it does not offer a DIY solution for its track lighting system. It is sold and installed through authorized dealers only.

faq.q: How much do Gemstone Lights cost per foot in Canada?
faq.a: Not published. Gemstone says pricing depends on linear footage and local installation rates and comes from a dealer quote. The only posted figure we found was one Colorado dealer at $28 per linear foot for fall 2026 (currency not stated, a US dealer), which is not a Canadian price.

faq.q: Is Gemstone's warranty better than the warranty on a DIY kit?
faq.a: It is longer. Gemstone lists a lifetime warranty on track lights and 10 years on system parts, with labour set by each dealer. Our kits carry a 5-year parts warranty and no lifetime cover.

faq.q: Are Gemstone Lights rated for Canadian winters?
faq.a: Gemstone lists operating temperature as "All North American Climates" and says the system was designed for Calgary winters, but it does not publish a figure in degrees. Our hardware is tested to -40 °C.

faq.q: Is a DIY track kit the same technology as Gemstone?
faq.a: It is the same category: 12V lights in an aluminum track under the eave, each light set individually from an app. Gemstone's lights are RGBWW at 9 inch spacing. Ours are RGBW at about 8 inches. The main differences are who installs it, the warranty length and whether the price is posted.
